title: 29th sitting of the 20th Majlis
summary: The sitting ran from 9:04 to 11:09 and was devoted to the preliminary debate on the government's bill to amend the Tourism Act (Law 2/99), sponsored by Abdulla Rasheed (Dhangethi). The bill changes how and when resort and guesthouse lessees pay fees to extend their lease periods. Members from the ruling side backed it as investor protection and a source of revenue; others asked what Maldivians gain, and several exchanges with the chair over points of order and relevance took up time. The bill was accepted for consideration 75 to 0 and sent to a committee of the whole Majlis, which was to meet the same day.

items.title: Attendance of the sitting
items.outcome: 51 members present at start, 2 on leave, 2 on official travel

items.title: Committee deadlines announced under Rule 174 (Finance Committee: Insurance Bill, Sovereign Development Fund Bill, State Fiscal Responsibility Bill, State Debt Bill)
items.outcome: Deadline of 30 October 2024 announced for all four

items.title: Preliminary debate on the bill to amend the Tourism Act (Law 2/99), sponsored by Abdulla Rasheed (Dhangethi)
items.outcome: debated; accepted for consideration 75-0-0 and sent to committee of the whole Majlis

speakers.name: Ahmed Didi
positions: Described the bill as a discount aimed at getting cash into the budget within six months.
Argued the government should instead market the Maldives to raise tourist arrivals; his remarks drew several points of order.

speakers.name: Mohamed Abbas
positions: Welcomed the bill and expected the committee stage to make the fee payment terms easier.
Criticised the MDP's approach to resort owners and defended resort staff conditions and taxes paid.
Exchanged remarks with the chair after points of order from other members.

speakers.name: Abdulla Rasheed
positions: As sponsor, said the bill lets lessees extend resort or guesthouse land leases for a fee and protects investors in the tourism industry.
In closing, urged members to take detailed debate to committee stage and pass the bill quickly.

speakers.name: Mauroof Zakir
positions: Said tourism should benefit Maldivians more, noted the high share of foreign staff, and called for progressive tax and further study of the amendment.
Raised a point of order objecting to how tourism workers were portrayed in the debate.

speakers.name: Yoosuf Nasheed
positions: Raised points of order saying the bill is not a discount but earlier payment, and that no extra money reaches the state unless an investor applies.

speakers.name: Mohamed Fazeel
positions: Raised points of order that the speaker was misdescribing the bill and that debate should stay on the bill.

speakers.name: Abdul Sattar Mohamed
positions: Supported the bill as a way to raise state revenue and give guesthouse operators and investors legal protection.

speakers.name: Mohamed Shahid
positions: Backed the bill, saying investors need legal protection and that the planned development bank would help local guesthouse and safari operators.

speakers.name: Abdul Gafoor Moosa
positions: Raised a point of order saying a speaker was misrepresenting the bill; the chair did not accept it as a point of order.

speakers.name: Hussain Ziyad
positions: Said the bill shortens the fee payment period to six months and he was unsure it was good or bad; urged priority for undeveloped islands and regions.
Raised concerns about the pace of legislation and worker opportunities.

speakers.name: Hassan Mufeed Abdul Gadir
positions: Supported the bill as a complete answer to investors' rights and said tourism is the backbone of the economy; criticised past calls to boycott it.

speakers.name: Mohamed Mamdooh
positions: Backed the bill, citing the number of resorts and beds in 2023 and saying investor certainty must be put in law.

speakers.name: Ahmed Naseer
positions: Supported the bill, said a strong judiciary is needed for investor confidence, and urged better marketing of the Maldives.

speakers.name: Ahmed Riyaz
positions: Supported the bill and asked the committee to make it easier to develop resorts in atolls that have none, including acquisition fees.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Hussain
positions: Argued Maldivians see too little benefit from the industry and called for resort income to flow through local banks and for equal pay for local staff.

speakers.name: Ameen Faisal
positions: Said Maldivian youth built the brand, asked what Maldivians get from a fee discount, and cautioned members against insulting each other.

speakers.name: Ahmed Aifan
positions: Raised a point of order that the speaker was straying from the bill and mentioned the debt left by the previous government.

speakers.name: Husnee Mubarik
positions: Said an MDP government changed the same law in 2020 with a lower fee and the window lapsed; called for audits of past lease deferrals.

decisions: Committee deadline of 30 October 2024 announced for the Insurance Bill, Sovereign Development Fund Bill, State Fiscal Responsibility Bill and State Debt Bill.
Bill to amend the Tourism Act (Law 2/99) accepted for consideration by 75 votes to 0.
Bill sent to a committee of the whole Majlis under Rule 106(r), to meet the same day.
Next sitting set for Monday 19 August 2024 at 9:00.

votes.what: Accept the Tourism Act (Law 2/99) amendment bill for consideration (76 present, 3 did not vote)
